proof_attempt_summary: Derived the informal matched 1/log(en) minimax supnorm frontier over every even cohort size and the full labeled exact-halfquota record, together with a donor result uniform over p in [1/4,1/2] and a polynomial-bit LP attainer. The field significance floor failed: score ceiling 7.0 versus 7.4, not salvageable within scope. Final math review flags a local omitted factor; independent D and MAIN audits verify that the existing half-difference supplies it, but the review caveat remains unrepaired and explicitly disclosed. No F-stage or Lean certification was performed.
tldr: The change in the fraction of public categories having exactly \(r\) buyers can be estimated simultaneously, in expected supnorm, at the sharp rate \(1/\log(en)\) under fixed categorical potential outcomes and exact-halfquota assignment. A parameter-free thinning followed by a canonical exact rational LP attains the rate with polynomial bit complexity. Explicit rational moment laws give an exact-total converse for every original-record randomized estimator, even with known constant controls. The same maximum-coefficient construction directly closes the Jana--Polyanskiy--Wu Appendix A.2 supnorm gap, uniformly over donor retention probabilities \(p\in[1/4,1/2]\).
gap: Jana--Polyanskiy--Wu Appendix A.2 leaves a factor of \(\log n\) between its supnorm bounds. A TV result does not decide whether one buyer frequency is as difficult as the entire profile.
fill: Maximum-coefficient calibration replaces an aggregate norm objective. Fixed unit blocks translate moment annihilation into equal full-record likelihoods. A verified thinning simulation supplies the upper benchmark while the lower route determines the scale.
